name: Mento Australian Dollar
oneLiner: AUDm is Mento's crypto-backed Australian dollar on Celo, minted by depositing USDm as Liquity-v2-style CDP collateral against the Mento reserve mix.
collateral: Mento V3 Liquity-v2-style CDPs collateralized by USDm; USDm in turn is backed by the Mento Reserve mix (sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, USDT, axlEUROC, stETH, and smaller positions exposed via the Mento reserve dashboard)
pegMechanism: Mento V3 oracle-priced FX stablecoin minted by depositing USDm as CDP collateral and borrowing AUDm against it; user-set interest rates, Stability Pool liquidations, and Liquity-style redemptions support the AUDm peg, with circuit breakers and Mento reserve transparency on the upstream USDm leg

oracleRisk.summary: AUDm's live Celo USDm/AUDm Broker exchange uses one SortedOracles reporter with a 360-second report-expiry window and minimumReports set to one; BreakerBox gates the swap but no second feed or failover path is configured.

branchApplicability.rationale: At Celo block 72127154, AUDm broker() returned the Mento v2 Broker and BiPoolManager exposed one USDm/AUDm exchange using rate feed 0x646bD504C3864Ea5b8A6B6D25743721f61864A07, minimumReports 1, and a 360-second reset/expiry window. SortedOracles had one reporter for that feed. The current Mento reserve API lists active CDP troves only for GBPm, JPYm, and CHFm, not AUDm, so AUDm has no live borrower-specific oracle/liquidation branch to enumerate.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Celo block 74313815 (2026-08-08T18:42:53Z), the sole tracked AUDm deployment 0x7175504c455076f15c04a2f90a8e352281f492f9 returned owner() = 0x890db8a597940165901372dd7db61c9f246e2147, broker() = 0x777a8255ca72412f0d706dc03c9d1987306b4cad, validators() = 0xaeb865bca93ddc8f47b8e29f40c5399ce34d0c58, and exchange() = zero. Its EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots still resolved to verified StableTokenV2 0x434563b0604be100f04b7ae485bcafe3c9d8850e and the Mento Timelock. The verified implementation exposes ordinary transfer/transferFrom, permissioned mint, broker/exchange-scoped burn, and Celo-VM-only gas debiting; it has no blacklist, freeze, pause, seizure, arbitrary-holder burn, or transfer-hook restriction. Mento's official materials describe direct protocol distribution and community governance with no single controlling entity, not a separate issuer freeze power. Direct holder freeze is therefore false; reserve-leg censorship and the timelocked upgrade path remain measured upstream and restrictability risks.

mintAuthority.summary: AUDm is minted via the Mento Broker (0x777A...) which is the sole authorized minter (broker() getter confirmed). The Broker's proxy admin and the AUDm token owner and proxy admin all resolve to the Mento Timelock (0x890DB...) with a 2-day delay.

controls.label: Mento Timelock — AUDm token owner and proxy admin
controls.evidence: At Celo block 69287341, owner() on AUDm returned 0x890DB8A597940165901372Dd7DB61C9f246e2147; EIP-1967 proxy admin slot returned the same address. getMinDelay() on the Timelock returned 0x2a300 = 172800 seconds (48 hours).

review.evidence: At Celo block 69287341: owner() = Timelock 0x890DB8A597940165901372Dd7DB61C9f246e2147 (confirmed); EIP-1967 proxy admin slot = same Timelock; getMinDelay() = 172800s (48h); broker() = 0x777A8255cA72412f0d706dc03C9D1987306B4CaD (Mento BrokerProxy, confirmed as sole authorized minter); Broker EIP-1967 proxy admin = same Timelock. Celo Registry confirms Broker = 0x777A... (keccak256('Broker') lookup). All mint-capable surfaces resolved. Economically, Broker issuance is the collateral-exchange path; changing that path or authorizing different mint logic requires the independently enforced 48-hour Mento Timelock, so the encoding-derived unbounded cap is superseded by raiseable semantics. Re-verified at Celo block 72664674 on 2026-07-20: AUDm 0x7175504C455076F15c04A2F90a8e352281f492F9 still returns owner() = Mento Timelock 0x890DB8A597940165901372Dd7DB61C9f246e2147 and broker() = 0x777A8255cA72412f0d706dc03C9D1987306B4CaD, and that Timelock still returns getMinDelay() = 172800 seconds. Mento publishes a live reserve dashboard rather than a periodic report, so reconciliation cadence is continuous (the self attestor tier is already recorded separately under proofOfReserves), and no financial regulator supervises Mento.

reserveReview.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-6 (lead usx-solstice)
reserveReview.rationale: AUDm is minted through Mento V3 CDPs collateralized in USDm, and USDm is backed by the shared Mento Reserve; the live mento adapter (breakerScope mento-reserve-audm) captures that shared reserve's constituent rows for AUDm, so the prior 100% USDm slice could not classify the captured CELO and stETH exposures. The envelope is restated at the constituent level on the adapter's exact identities and 2026-07-20 captured weights from the issuer-run reserve analytics API ($19.12M total, grouped across chains and custodians); the USDm CDP leg is described in the collateral field and is not duplicated as a second layer. Each stablecoin constituent links to its tracked asset, and CELO, stETH, and the residual ETH dust now carry explicit classification and failure-domain identity. The live adapter refreshes weights at runtime.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Mento reserve analytics API constituent identities and weights captured 2026-07-20; AUDm CDP collateral is USDm, whose backing is this shared reserve mix
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Every constituent of the shared Mento Reserve captured by the live adapter is identified and either linked to a tracked stablecoin or explicitly classified. Constituent weights drift and are refreshed by the live adapter.

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-6 (lead usx-solstice)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Reserve assets backing USDm (and transitively AUDm) are held in on-chain Mento Reserve safes, liquidity contracts, operational accounts, and governance-approved strategies rather than with a legal custodian, so legal segregation, insolvency treatment, and strategy-specific reuse limits are not established by the reviewed sources; constituent-level custody (e.g. Circle, Tether, Agora, Sky, Lido) sits with each issuer.
